race_overlay.heat: July in Idaho Springs, Colorado can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Bob Cook Memorial Mt. Blue Sky Hill Climb (formerly Mt. Evans). Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan that matches the ride duration, intensity, weather, and confirmed resupply points.
race_overlay.altitude: Bob Cook Memorial Mt. Blue Sky Hill Climb (formerly Mt. Evans) with 6,590ft of climbing finishes high enough for reduced oxygen availability to affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Temperature drop of 30-40F from start to summit — hypothermia is a real risk; 40%+ reduction in oxygen at the summit — breathing is labored even standing still.
